What is Rails: Ruby on Rails (often just Rails) is a full-stack web application framework written in Ruby by David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH). It follows the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architectural pattern and emphasizes convention over configuration, DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself), and rapid development. Rails includes everything needed to build database-backed web applications: ORM (ActiveRecord), routing, templating, testing, asset pipeline, and more. First released in 2004, Rails popularized many modern web development practices.

# Install Rails
gem install rails
rails --version

# Create new app
rails new myapp
cd myapp

# Generate scaffold (model + views + controller + migrations)
rails generate scaffold Post title:string body:text

# Run migrations
rails db:migrate

# Start server
rails server
# Visit http://localhost:3000/posts
MVC Architecture: Rails follows the Model-View-Controller pattern. Models (ActiveRecord) handle data and business logic. Views (ActionView) render HTML/JSON templates. Controllers (ActionController) process requests, interact with models, and render views. The router maps URLs to controller actions. Additional layers: mailers, helpers, channels, jobs, libraries.

Project Structure: A Rails project has a standardized directory structure. app/ contains models, views, controllers, helpers, jobs, mailers, channels. config/ has routes, database, environments. db/ holds migrations and schema. public/ serves static assets. test/ (or spec/) for tests. Gemfile lists dependencies. The rails command and Rake tasks handle most development operations.

Models & ORM: ActiveRecord is Rails' Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) layer. Each model class maps to a database table. Instances map to rows. Columns become attributes automatically. Convention: table names are plural snake_case, model names are singular CamelCase. Foreign keys: user_id. Primary keys: id (auto-increment). ActiveRecord handles CRUD, validations, associations, queries, and migrations.

# app/models/user.rb
class User < ApplicationRecord
  # Automatically maps to 'users' table
  # Columns 'id', 'name', 'email', 'created_at', 'updated_at'
end

# Create
user = User.create(name: "Alice", email: "alice@example.com")

# Read
user = User.find(1)
users = User.where(active: true)
user = User.find_by(email: "alice@example.com")

# Update
user.update(name: "Alice Smith")

# Delete
user.destroy

# Query methods
User.where("created_at > ?", 1.week.ago)
User.order(name: :asc).limit(10)
User.select(:id, :name).distinct
User.includes(:posts).all  # Eager loading
Validations: Validations ensure data integrity before saving to the database. Common validators: presence, uniqueness, length, format, numericality, inclusion, acceptance, confirmation. Custom validations via validate or custom validator classes. Validations run automatically on create/save/update. Check validity with valid?/invalid? which populate errors.errors.full_messages.

class User < ApplicationRecord
  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :email, presence: true,
                   uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false },
                   format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP }
  validates :age, numericality: { greater_than: 0, less_than: 150 }
  validates :terms, acceptance: true
  validates :password, length: { minimum: 8, maximum: 128 }

  # Custom validation
  validate :email_domain_allowed

  private

  def email_domain_allowed
    allowed = ["example.com", "rails.org"]
    domain = email&.split("@")&.last
    if domain && !allowed.include?(domain)
      errors.add(:email, "domain not allowed")
    end
  end
end

# Usage
user = User.new(email: "test@invalid.com")
unless user.valid?
  puts user.errors.full_messages
end
Associations: ActiveRecord associations define relationships between models. Types: belongs_to, has_many, has_one, has_many :through, has_one :through, has_and_belongs_to_many (HABTM). Polymorphic associations allow a model to belong to multiple models. Dependent options: :destroy, :delete_all, :nullify, :restrict_with_error. Counter cache for performance.

class Post < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :author, class_name: "User"
  has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :tags, through: :taggings
  has_one :featured_image, as: :imageable  # polymorphic
end

class Comment < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :post, counter_cache: true
  belongs_to :user
end

class User < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :posts, foreign_key: :author_id
  has_many :comments
end

class Tag < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :taggings
  has_many :posts, through: :taggings
end

# Usage
post = Post.first
post.author          # User object
post.comments        # Collection of comments
post.tags            # Tags through taggings

user = User.first
user.posts           # User's posts (via author_id)

# Eager loading
posts = Post.includes(:author, :comments).all
Migrations: Migrations are versioned changes to the database schema. Rails tracks which migrations have run via schema_migrations table. Key generators: rails generate migration, rails generate model. Migration methods: create_table, change_table, add_column, remove_column, change_column, add_index, remove_index, create_join_table, add_reference, change_table. Rollback with rails db:rollback.

# Generate a migration
# rails generate migration AddPublishedToPosts published:boolean

class AddPublishedToPosts < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.0]
  def change
    add_column :posts, :published, :boolean, default: false
    add_index :posts, :published
  end
end

# Create table
# rails generate migration CreateCategories name:string slug:string:uniq

class CreateCategories < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.0]
  def change
    create_table :categories do |t|
      t.string :name, null: false
      t.string :slug, null: false
      t.text :description
      t.timestamps
    end
    add_index :categories, :slug, unique: true
  end
end

# Commands
# rails db:migrate         # Run pending
# rails db:rollback        # Undo last
# rails db:migrate:status  # Show status
# rails db:schema:dump     # Update schema.rb

Routes & Resources: config/routes.rb defines URL patterns. The router maps HTTP verbs + paths to controller actions. resources generates RESTful routes (index, show, new, create, edit, update, destroy). singular_resource for non-ID routes. Nested resources for hierarchical data. Member and collection routes for custom actions. Concerns share reusable route groups.

# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  # RESTful resources
  resources :posts
  resources :users

  # Nested resources
  resources :posts do
    resources :comments
  end

  # Custom routes
  get "/about", to: "pages#about"
  get "/search", to: "search#show"

  # Namespaced (admin area)
  namespace :admin do
    resources :users
  end

  # Member and collection
  resources :posts do
    member do
      post :publish
    end
    collection do
      get :drafts
    end
  end

  # Root route
  root "posts#index"
end

# Generated routes:
# GET    /posts           posts#index
# GET    /posts/new       posts#new
# POST   /posts           posts#create
# GET    /posts/:id       posts#show
# GET    /posts/:id/edit  posts#edit
# PATCH  /posts/:id       posts#update
# DELETE /posts/:id       posts#destroy

# Check routes: rails routes

ActionController: Controllers process HTTP requests. Each public method is an action. params hash contains request data (query string, form data, URL segments). Strong parameters protect against mass assignment. Filters (before_action, after_action, around_action) run before/after actions. Flash messages for user notifications. Session and cookies for state. Respond_to for content negotiation.

class PostsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_post, only: [:show, :edit, :update, :destroy]
  before_action :authenticate_user!, except: [:index, :show]

  def index
    @posts = Post.published.order(created_at: :desc)
  end

  def show
  end

  def new
    @post = Post.new
  end

  def create
    @post = current_user.posts.build(post_params)
    if @post.save
      redirect_to @post, notice: "Post created!"
    else
      render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  def update
    if @post.update(post_params)
      redirect_to @post, notice: "Post updated!"
    else
      render :edit, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @post.destroy
    redirect_to posts_path, notice: "Post deleted!"
  end

  private

  def set_post
    @post = Post.find(params[:id])
  end

  def post_params
    params.require(:post).permit(:title, :body, :published)
  end
end
Strong Parameters: Strong Parameters protect against mass assignment vulnerabilities. params.require(:model) ensures the key exists. .permit(:field1, :field2) whitelists allowed attributes. Nested parameters require nested permit. Arrays, hashes, and scalars have different permit syntax. Never trust user input — always whitelist permitted parameters.

class UsersController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @user = User.new(user_params)
    # ...
  end

  private

  def user_params
    params.require(:user).permit(
      :name, :email, :password, :password_confirmation,
      :avatar, :bio,
      role_ids: [],
      address_attributes: [:street, :city, :zip]
    )
  end
end

# Fetch params hash
# params = ActionController::Parameters.new({
#   user: { name: "Alice", admin: true }
# })
# user_params would return { name: "Alice" }
# (admin is NOT permitted)

ERB Templates: ActionView renders templates. Default template engine is ERB (.html.erb). <% %> executes Ruby code without output. <%= %> executes and outputs. Layouts wrap templates (yield). Partials (_partial.html.erb) share reusable view fragments. Helpers keep templates clean. Content_for yields named content. Link_to, form_for, image_tag are common view helpers.

Form Helpers: Rails form helpers generate HTML forms with CSRF protection, error handling, and correct field names. form_for / form_with (Rails 5.1+). form_with can work with models or URLs. Collection helpers: collection_select, collection_check_boxes. Date/time select helpers. Fields for nested attributes. Strong parameters integration.

Rails Testing: Rails supports Minitest natively (test/ directory) and RSpec (via gem). Test types: unit tests (models), functional tests (controllers), integration tests (full stack), system tests (browser with Capybara). Fixtures and factories (FactoryBot) for test data. Assertions: assert_equal, assert_response, assert_redirected_to, assert_select, assert_difference.

# test/models/post_test.rb (Minitest)
require "test_helper"

class PostTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "should not save without title" do
    post = Post.new
    assert_not post.save, "Saved without a title"
  end

  test "should have comments counter" do
    post = posts(:one)
    assert_difference("post.comments.count", 1) do
      post.comments.create!(body: "Nice!", user: users(:alice))
    end
  end
end

# test/controllers/posts_controller_test.rb
class PostsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @post = posts(:one)
  end

  test "should get index" do
    get posts_url
    assert_response :success
  end

  test "should create post" do
    assert_difference("Post.count") do
      post posts_url, params: {
        post: { title: "Test", body: "Body" }
      }
    end
    assert_redirected_to post_path(Post.last)
  end
end
